name: cart_items
title: Cart Items
description: One product in one basket, with the price it carried when it went in. Stamping the price at add-time is what lets the shop notice later that it moved: a price that changes while somebody is shopping must not silently change what they thought they were agreeing to, and a basket that has sat for three weeks must not hold the seller to a stale price either. Both numbers are kept and the DISAGREEMENT is surfaced at checkout (object_cart.price_changes) rather than resolved in secret in either direction -- the same instinct as stamping a rate at approval and refusing to let a later change restate it (docs/logic-decisions.md #1). No stock is reserved by anything here: availability is decided at checkout, because reserving on add is how a shop shows 'sold out' for goods nobody bought.

fields.name: description
fields.label: Description
fields.help: Stamped from the product name so a basket still reads correctly if the product is later renamed.

fields.name: quantity
fields.label: Quantity
fields.help: May be fractional -- 1.5 kg, 2.5 hours of setup -- so line money is Decimal arithmetic rounded once per line.

fields.name: unit_price_cents
fields.label: Unit Price
fields.help: What it cost when it went in the basket, in integer minor units. Compared against the live price at checkout, never quietly replaced by it.
